# LTeN-CNRS / Nantes Université — Laboratoire de Thermique et Énergie de Nantes

## Why it matters internationally

LTeN is a smaller but clearly active French node whose importance lies in
**thematic modernity**. Architectured ceramics and related structured
materials are exactly the types of systems for which emissivity can no
longer be treated as a fixed, scalar background parameter. Instead it
becomes a **designable property**, linked to porosity, geometry, scale
hierarchy, and spectral response. Laboratories like LTeN carry emissivity
work into the domain of materials architecture and functional
microstructure, where the problem becomes not only measurement but
**interpretation and design**.

## Scope of activity

### Relevant activity

- **LTeN — high-temperature radiative properties of architectured
  ceramics.** The group works on emissivity characterization of structured
  ceramics at high temperature and on modeling of emissivity for CeO₂
  ceramics (traceable in CNRS/HAL records).

### Radiative properties measured

High-temperature emissivity of architectured ceramics — with explicit
attention to the geometric and microstructural factors that control it.

### Capability envelope

- **Temperature:** high temperature.
- **Methodology:** high-temperature emissivity characterization of
  architectured ceramics; modeling of emissivity of CeO₂ ceramics;
  integration of measurement with structural/architectural descriptors of
  the material.

### Application domains

- Architectured ceramics
- Functional microstructure and structured materials where emissivity is
  linked to porosity, geometry, and spectral response
- Materials where emissivity engineering is part of the design problem

## IR-EMPOWER contributions

- **Léo Gaillard** — high-temperature emissivity characterization of
  architectured ceramics.

## Why LTeN-CNRS is a reference pole

Once a material is designed rather than merely sampled, the emissivity
measurement has to cope with the full heterogeneity of its architecture —
porosity gradients, surface texture, unit-cell geometry. LTeN is one of
the laboratories bringing this viewpoint into high-temperature
measurement, which makes it a natural bridge between the classical
emissivity community and the rapidly growing engineered-emissivity
community represented in Tier III.
